text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for high blood pressure (hypertension) include lifestyle changes, prescription medications, and medical procedures.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, prescription medications, and medical procedures

text_blocks.snippet: Adopting a heart-healthy routine is the first step or a helpful companion to medication:

list.snippet: DASH Eating Plan: Focus on fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while cutting back on saturated fat and cholesterol.
Reduce Sodium: Limit salt intake to under 2,000 mg (or ideally under 1,500 mg) per day.
Physical Activity: Engage in regular aerobic exercise, such as walking, swimming, or biking, for at least 2.5 hours per week.
Weight Management: Lose excess weight if you have overweight or obesity.
Limit Alcohol and Quit Smoking: Reduce alcohol consumption and stop smoking or using tobacco products.
Improve Sleep: Aim for at least 7 hours of quality sleep per night.

text_blocks.snippet: When lifestyle changes alone do not lower blood pressure below the target goal (typically under 130/80 mm Hg for most adults), doctors prescribe medications:

list.snippet: ACE Inhibitors & ARBs: Relax and widen blood vessels (e.g., lisinopril, losartan).
Calcium Channel Blocker (CCBs): Prevent calcium from entering muscle cells in the heart and blood vessels to keep them relaxed (e.g., amlodipine).
Diuretics ("Water Pills"): Help the body remove excess sodium and water (e.g., thiazide diuretics like hydrochlorothiazide).

Other Options: Beta-blockers, alpha-blockers, central-acting agents, or vasodilators may be added depending on other health conditions like heart failure or kidney disease. Many patients need a combination of two or more drugs, sometimes combined into a single pill.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed drug classes through the American Heart Association.

list.snippet: Renal Denervation: A minimally invasive, FDA-approved procedure that targets nerves in the arteries leading to the kidneys to help lower blood pressure in patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension.
